pairs.subject: retry-backoff
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/webhook-idempotency.ts:18 The only retry-shaped code in this context sits on the receiving side of other systems' retries. A dedupe store failure returns the retryable class (5xx) instead of letting the request through unchecked. The claim key makes a sender's retried write safe, and that claim survives a restart and has a named reaper, so no technique here is a deviation; ladder, breaker, redirect, revocation and suspension machinery do not exist in these files.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/webhook-idempotency.ts:18 A store error fails closed with a 5xx, which tells the sender to retry. The receiver dedupes on the provider's Idempotency-Key, or else on a body hash (line 44), so the sender's ambiguous write is dedup-keyed downstream, as the timeout rule requires.

app/_lib/webhook-idempotency.ts:10 The dedupe identity is a persisted row, not a process Map, so a replay after a crash is still recognised. It is claimed before the side effects run, and it has explicit reapers: a 15-minute lease for in-flight claims (line 22) and a 7-day done-horizon.

app/_lib/ops-telemetry.ts:132 The exhausted terminal state of the comms outbox (dead letters) appears on the ops surface as a count with a stated predicate (status failed) and window (7 days), never as a bare number.
app/_lib/webhook-idempotency.ts:80 The retry schedule belongs to the external sender. These files compute no delay ladder, and a grep for backoff and jitter finds nothing in them.

app/_lib/sentry-client.ts:68 The single outbound call in this context (Sentry) is one fire-and-forget attempt with no retry, so there is no repeated calling for a breaker to stop. A grep for circuit and breaker finds no breaker.
